title: Repurposing amlexanox as a topical anti-inflammatory and antioxidant intervention for diabetic foot ulcers: insights from in-silico and in-vivo studies.
authors: Kapoor, Nishika; Dhaliwal, Navneet; Dhaliwal, Jatinder; Chopra, Kanwaljit
one_liner_zh: 该文研究阿米洛克斯对糖尿病足溃疡的抗炎抗氧化作用，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或MD方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs), a debilitating manifestation of diabetes mellitus, involve persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, and impaired wound healing, largely driven by NF-kappaB overactivation. Amlexanox (ALX), a synthetic anti-inflammatory and antioxidant agent, was evaluated for its therapeutic potential in DFUs. METHODS: In-silico molecular docking and pharmacokinetic studies were conducted to predict ALX's interactions with major DFU targets and to assess its topical suitability. STZ-induced diabetic rats with full-thickness foot ulcers (5 mm) received topical ALX (2.5% and 5%) or silver sulfadiazine ointments for 14 days. Wound closure, antioxidant enzymes, oxidative stress markers, connective tissue markers, pro-inflammatory markers and NF-kappaB expression were assessed in the wound tissue. RESULTS: ALX demonstrated strong binding to the pathological targets (NF-kappaB, MMP-9, MPO, and COX-2) and displayed a favourable PK profile. Moreover, ALX topical treatment did not normalise diabetic metabolic alterations, but it dose-dependently promoted wound healing. Indeed, ALX 5% significantly accelerated wound closure (p < 0.0001) and led to marked suppression of NF-kappaB and MMP-9 expression (p < 0.0001). It also enhanced the levels of connective tissue markers, including hexosamine (p < 0.001), hydroxyproline, and hexuronic acid (p < 0.0001). Robust anti-inflammatory effects were also observed, as ALX reduced IL-1beta, IL-6, TNF-alpha levels and COX-2 activity (p < 0.0001). Furthermore, ALX 5% diminished oxidative stress by lowering LPO, PCO, and MPO levels (p < 0.0001), and restoring GSH levels and SOD and CAT (p < 0.001) activities indicating its anti-oxidant properties. CONCLUSION: Taken together, the present work highlights the mechanisms associated with ALX mediated wound healing in diabetic rats thereby demonstrating its potential as a promising strategy for DFU management.
abstract_zh: 背景：糖尿病足溃疡（DFUs）是糖尿病的一种致残性表现，涉及持续炎症、氧化应激和伤口愈合受损，主要由NF-kappaB过度激活驱动。本研究评估了合成抗炎和抗氧化剂氨来占诺（ALX）在DFUs中的治疗潜力。方法：进行了计算机模拟分子对接和药代动力学研究，以预测ALX与主要DFU靶点的相互作用并评估其局部用药适用性。对链脲佐菌素（STZ）诱导的糖尿病大鼠造成全层足部溃疡（5 mm），分别给予局部ALX（2.5%和5%）或磺胺嘧啶银软膏治疗14天。评估伤口组织中伤口闭合、抗氧化酶、氧化应激标志物、结缔组织标志物、促炎标志物及NF-kappaB表达。结果：ALX与病理靶点（NF-kappaB、MMP-9、MPO和COX-2）表现出强结合，并显示出良好的药代动力学特征。此外，ALX局部治疗未使糖尿病代谢异常正常化，但剂量依赖性地促进伤口愈合。确实，ALX 5%显著加速伤口闭合（p < 0.0001），并显著抑制NF-kappaB和MMP-9表达（p < 0.0001）。它还提高了结缔组织标志物水平，包括己糖胺（p < 0.001）、羟脯氨酸和己糖醛酸（p < 0.0001）。同时观察到强效抗炎作用，ALX降低了IL-1beta、IL-6、TNF-alpha水平和COX-2活性（p < 0.0001）。此外，ALX 5%通过降低LPO、PCO和MPO水平（p < 0.0001）并恢复GSH水平及SOD和CAT活性（p < 0.001）来减轻氧化应激，表明其抗氧化特性。结论：综合来看，本研究阐明了ALX介导糖尿病大鼠伤口愈合的相关机制，从而证明其作为DFU管理有前景策略的潜力。
